name: Lake View Hotel Restaurant
why_it_matters: The longest-running hotel-restaurant on Nako lake (4.5/5 Google, 'Excellent' on Tripadvisor as of 2026), run by the family who later opened Nako Regency. Every table looks straight onto the lake and the Reo Purgyil massif beyond — the dining room is the view, not the food.
insider_tip: Stick to thukpa, momos and rajma chawal — items that need fresh boiling water do well at 3,660m; complex tandoor or fried plates are hit-or-miss. Order the local seabuckthorn juice if it's on the day's stock.
signature_address: Lake View Hotel, edge of Nako Lake, Nako village, Kinnaur 172114

name: Hotel Nako Regency Restaurant
why_it_matters: Nako's newest dining room (opened 2023 by the Lake View Hotel family) — a 50-seater finished entirely in polished Kinnauri timber, with 8am-10pm hours that are unusual for a 600-person village. Wide windows frame Reo Purgyil. The pizza is a recurring surprise pick in reviews for somewhere this remote.
insider_tip: Last orders are 9pm — earlier than feels right at altitude. The kitchen is the most reliable bet on the road between Sangla and Tabo, so plan a long lunch here if your itinerary allows.
signature_address: Hotel Nako Regency, Nako village, Kinnaur 172114

name: Reo Purguil Hotel Restaurant
why_it_matters: A small hotel-restaurant named after Himachal's highest peak (Reo Purgyil, 6,816m), serving the basic Spiti-Kinnaur menu plus Himachali staples like chana madra and siddu that the higher-end Nako restaurants skip. Where most pre-booked tour groups passing through stop for lunch.
insider_tip: Ask for siddu if it's available — the steamed Himachali stuffed bread is the dish you can't reliably get further inside Spiti, and it's the local Kinnauri specialty.
signature_address: Reo Purguil Hotel, Nako village, Kinnaur 172114
